# Source permission ownership for a generated JSP button

The form retains the already supported finance-detail-generation fixture's
cross-fragment program so intake must recognize a real translated JSP control,
rather than accepting a handcrafted button or permission marker. The button is
inside a source `right` section: `N2=edit`, `n2=hidden`, `N72=edit`, `N3=view`.
The paired workflow has one canonical `N2`, so existing restrictive case-conflict
resolution must preserve `hidden` for drafting and `edit` for `N72`.

The route test checks Source Draft, DSL, fake execution and independent native
authority readback. Its captured `useAuth` replay explicitly supplies the
persisted node permission as the auth input; it does not claim that a real
server/new-document screen selected that node. The button action is not clicked,
and the global `editShow` add/edit permission contract is unchanged.

Unrecognized handlers, a button outside the permission section, duplicate
fragment identities and a renamed generated identity cover ownership boundaries.
